name: Investment Adviser
title: SEBI Registered Investment Adviser (RIA)
intro: From graduation to a SEBI Registered Investment Adviser: NISM Series X-A and X-B, SEBI registration under the Investment Advisers Regulations, then a fee-only advisory practice.

phases.title: Graduate
phases.summary: Any discipline; finance, commerce or economics helps.
points: A graduate degree in any discipline is enough — SEBI relaxed the earlier postgraduate requirement in its December 2024 amendments.
Commerce, finance or economics helps with the content.
Any Class 12 stream can lead here.

phases.title: NISM Series X-A (Level 1)
phases.summary: Basics of personal finance and regulation.
points: NISM Series X-A is the Investment Adviser (Level 1) certification.
It covers the basics of personal finance and regulation.
It is a required step before X-B.

phases.title: NISM Series X-B (Level 2)
points: NISM Series X-B is the Investment Adviser (Level 2) certification.
It covers advanced financial planning and advisory.
Keep both certifications valid as SEBI requires.

phases.title: Apply to SEBI
phases.summary: Registration as an individual Investment Adviser.
points: Apply under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 as amended.
Meet SEBI's fit-and-proper criteria and the deposit and other registration conditions.
CFA and financial-planning credentials add depth but are not SEBI registration.

phases.title: Build a fee-only practice
points: RIAs charge clients a fee for advice; mutual-fund distributors earn commissions — SEBI keeps the two separate.
Independent RIAs build income slowly as the client base grows; advisory firms also hire certified staff.
Growth path: associate → RIA → principal of an advisory firm.
